chunks: Until when he comes before Us he will say: 'Would to God there was a distance of the East and West between you and me, for you were an evil companion!'

key_terms.بُعْدَ الْمَشْرِقَيْنِ: distance of the two Easts (East and West)

ai.seo_question: What does the sinner say to Shaytan on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In this verse from Surah Az-Zukhruf, the repentant sinner expresses deep regret at the Day of Judgment, wishing for the maximum possible distance from Shaytan, whom he now recognizes as a clear enemy. Shia exegetes, such as Allamah Tabatabai, highlight that this regret comes too late for salvation, emphasizing the finality of one's choices and the deceptive nature of evil companionship. The phrase 'bad companion' (bi'sa al-qarin) underscores the personal accountability for those who followed misguidance, a theme central to Shia eschatology regarding the separation of the righteous from the deviant.
